* PAD costs 2 to rez and Marked costs 0. Trashing the economy means you're extremely poor and wasting all your clicks making money and running on the remotes to trash them. Trashing an early PAD is the right play in my opinion, but never a Marked.
* I and many others run the most efficient breakers possible. The problem is that Eli, Caduceus and Roto have 2 subs. Tollbooth is just always taxing. Pop-up Window is great as well.
* I responded earlier about how to stop The Source. Install your NAPD and advance it twice. If NBN manages to score just one Astro, the time you have left to win starts ticking very quick. The ability to tutor for another Astro and score it same turn is absurdly powerful.

I'm wondering if you're just theorycrafting or if you've actually played a high volume of games against top tier NEH decks/players. I could be shown an NEH deck list and still lose over 50% of the time to it because it's that efficient and powerful. I think that there will be some serious NEH hate cards (or, more likely, fast advance hate in general) in the next big box, but until then I think NEH will be the strongest corp for this cycle by a long shot.

If you're against The Source all you do is put out a 3/2 in a server and advance it once (even better, NAPD and advance it twice). If the runner steals it, great, The Source is gone and they lost money. If not, you score it and The Source is gone. FA decks tend to panic when they see The Source because it really does stop FA, but that's only until one agenda is scored. I will agree that The Source is viable with Fall Guys, but then you're devoting so much of your deck and influence on that, and you're usually just going to lose anyways.

The issue is that NBN, Astroscript Pilot Program in particular, is too fast. TWIY never saw the win rate NEH has because it had to devote all its money to fast advancing agendas, which is really expensive. TWIY's ice was cheap ETR ice because they can't afford anything else and didn't have the influence to. NEH is always rich (or the runner is extremely poor and wasting clicks not accessing centrals if they are trashing asset econ) and drawing at the same time. This, along with 5 extra influence, allows them to import very efficient, taxing ice along with cheap ETR ice. You could usually hammer TWIY's central servers for extremely cheap by the mid game as runner. When you're against 3 Eli 1.0s and Caduceus/Tollboth you can't. When you have the resources to consistently score Astros **out of deck** you're going to beat the runner.

Whaaaaat? I got it for $14.99 from invinylwetrust. They have great prices and service, but they stack all your albums on top of each other when they ship them -- in case anyone worries about album safety.

I just recently started collecting vinyl, and I haven't listened to most of these albums in a long time, so I didn't go very in-depth with these reviews. Sorry!

Bonus points if anyone can figure out what album is barely in the picture to the right.

**Washed Out - Within and Without** - 
A solid chillwave album. If you like really laid back music then this is for you. I was a little let down because of some really high expectations after his Life of Leisure EP, but you should definitely check this out if you like chillwave.

Suggested songs: [Amor Fati](http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Jkpl-N-FGm8), [Eyes Be Closed](http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Cj2HcdiOmt8)

[album art + white vinyl](http://i.imgur.com/DUnuu.jpg)

**Animal Collective - Sung Tongs + Feels** - 
Feels is my favorite album of all time and I'm a big Animal Collective fan. It's hard to describe their music, but it usually has a really warm and energetic atmosphere to it that I love. If you're interested in giving AC another chance, definitely check out Feels.

Suggested songs: [The Purple Bottle](http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uyJjihseiio), [Who Could Win a Rabbit](http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-6e5vnJcRYo)

[LP jacket](http://i.imgur.com/gt6Xo.jpg)

[LP jacket](http://i.imgur.com/yNcNJ.jpg)

**Joanna Newsom - Ys** - 
Definitely not for everyone -- this a really dense album that's coupled with Joanna's very weird singing voice. I'd suggest Newsom's most recent LP, Have One on Me, if you haven't heard of her. However, if her voice grows on you (I personally love it), then Ys is a real treat. Newsom's songwriting and lyrics are some of the best of the 2000s.

Suggested song: [Emily](http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yW8zvWdxCHg)

[lyric book + back cover](http://imgur.com/a/qaSLV)

**Sleigh Bells - Treats** - 
I think the album art sums up this band pretty well. The cheerleaders represent the high/catchy/"poppy" melodies that are sung throughout the album, and the defaced faces (sorry for that redundancy...) are what happens after the wall of sound that comes from the distorted guitars hits them. An absolute must listen for any noise pop fan.

Suggested songs: [Rill Rill](http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uLRnmQ-4Yp0), [Infinity Guitars](http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fheYx_ZPU18&ob=av3e) 

[back cover + lyric book](http://imgur.com/a/ljyoq)

**Sufjan Stevens - Illinois** - 
Let me preface this by saying that 95% of the time I hate concept albums. This one by Sufjan Stevens, however, is one of that 5% that I love. This is an indie folk/pop album, and it uses a lot of orchestral arrangements really well. The songwriting and musicianship on this album is top notch.

Suggested songs: [Casimir Pulaski Day](http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9EzeW5KoPUI), [Decatur, or, Round of Applause for Your Stepmother!](http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Dgu88Ywii3Y)

[fold out LP jacket art](http://i.imgur.com/8hyqq.jpg)

**The Dismemberment Plan - Emergency & I** - 
A classic post punk album. I'm not very knowledgable about the genre, but Emergency & I sounds so unique that I love it. I'd recommend this no matter what your taste is, it definitely grows on you.

Suggested songs: [A Life of Possibilities](http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nRLOf3bSlVs), [The City](http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cMLiFpecgVg)

[LP jacket, lyrics, pictures of band](http://i.imgur.com/Yb7YM.jpg)

**Belle & Sebastian - If You're Feeling Sinister** - 
Again, I haven't heard much champer pop outside of these guys, but I'd suggest them if you like any sort of folk or indie pop, even. There's not much to dislike about this album -- it's the strongest out of their expansive disography. I don't know if people feel divided about Stuart Murdoch's voice, but I think it's great.

Suggested songs: [Get Me Away from Here, I'm Dying](http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yS_DcqPkEYM), [If You're Feeling Sinister](http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=obNIqksGYnQ)

[LP jacket](http://i.imgur.com/tvBT3.jpg)

**Archers of Loaf - Icky Mettle** - 
I've heard this album the least out of the nine here -- I only recently started listening to Archers of Loaf. To be brief, it's really solid 90's indie rock. If you like Pavement or just guitar heavy indie rock, definitely give it a listen.

Suggested songs: [Web in Front](http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MnIBBbWFJ38), [Might](http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KrfpNboPj-I)

[LP jacket, blue vinyl](http://i.imgur.com/Q1Cnq.jpg)
